newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: US envoy Richardson slams Iraq on hidden weapons.
newsitem.headline: US envoy Richardson slams Iraq on hidden weapons.

text.p: Bill Richardson, the new U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, on Monday slammed Iraq for its "intransigence" in not coming clean on its weapons of mass destruction.

In a written statement to the council, he said "This is our 36th review of the sanctions against Iraq. And for the 36th time Iraq has failed to comply with its obligations under Security Council resolutions."
His hardline statement was handed to the press as the council reviewed the sanctions but left them intact. Destroying weapons of mass destruction is a key requirement for lifting the oil embargo.
He said the four-month confrontation, recently resolved, over handing over to U.N. inspectors 130 Scud rocket motors unearthed last November was pointless.

"Let there be no doubt of the importance of this incident. The tests to be carried out on the motors and missile parts will be essential in determining Iraq's current missile capabilities, including whether Iraq is maintaining an operational force of prosecribed missiles with unconventional warheads," he said.
He said U.N. inspectors believed "that Iraq continues to maintain just such a force."

Richardson said that the incident would never have occured in the first place had Iraq complied with its obligation. "The bottom line is that there is no change in Iraq's obstructionism towards UNSCOM (the U.N. Special Commission in charge of disarming Iraq), " he said.
"Iraq's approach still requires Chairman Ekeus to expend considerable effort to obligat Iraq to take each small, gruding step toward complaince."

He said that Iraq's behavior inspired no confidence but highlighted the need for continued vigilence. "We fully expect that Iraq will seek to challenge the council's authority again in the future," he concluded.
